summary: EASD 2026 opens today in Milan (28 Sep–2 Oct), so the next 5 days are packed with GLP-1 news. The best early opportunities are the retatrutide phase 3 results in type 2 diabetes (TRIUMPH-2, symposium on Sep 30), the Danish/UK EASD analysis arguing that people with a BMI of 25–26.9 plus inflammation or high remnant cholesterol may qualify for heart protection, and CagriSema vs tirzepatide (REIMAGINE 5). Coverage of REIMAGINE 5 is thin and often misleading, because the tirzepatide arm used the 5 mg dose. The strongest carry-over story is the WashU VA study on stopping GLP-1s and cardiovascular risk. It needs the "never change your medicine without your prescriber" framing. Side-effect questions are rising in consumer search: hair loss, menstrual changes, NAION/vision lawsuits, and people who respond less well to the drugs. They work best as calm, evidence-first explainers. Two peer-reviewed signals that few creators are covering yet fit our "getting the most from GLP-1" pillar: the STEP UP thigh-muscle MRI analysis and the Clin Nutr piece on creatine and GLP-1 muscle loss. Two items are rejected: microdosing (MindBodyGreen, Yahoo) and anything that promotes compounded or research-chemical retatrutide.

candidates.topic: Retatrutide phase 3 in type 2 diabetes: TRIUMPH-2 showed up to 20.8% average weight loss and up to 1.6% lower A1C at 80 weeks (EASD symposium, Sep 30)
candidates.angle: What a 'triple agonist' (GIP + GLP-1 + glucagon) is, in plain words. What TRIUMPH-2 showed in adults with type 2 diabetes and overweight or obesity. Why it isn't approved yet, and why gray-market 'retatrutide' vials (see the Philippine FDA advisory) are a real danger, not a shortcut.
candidates.predicted_peak: 2–6 days (after the Sep 30 symposium and full data release)
candidates.why_now: EASD opens today. Lilly has confirmed a phase 3 retatrutide symposium on Sep 30, and consumer searches for retatrutide are already high because of gray-market hype. Once full data land, mainstream coverage will follow within days.

evidence.signal: Lilly will present Foundayo, retatrutide and eloraTZP data at EASD 2026. TRIUMPH-2: up to 22.5 kg (20.8%) average weight loss and up to 1.6% lower A1C at 80 weeks
Retatrutide diabetes results lead the EASD 2026 opening
Public warning against unregistered 'Retatrutide 30 mg' powder for injection

candidates.topic: BMI 25–26.9 but high heart risk: EASD 2026 Danish/UK analysis says about half of this 'not eligible' group has coronary heart disease risk similar to people who qualify for GLP-1s
candidates.angle: 'Overweight but not eligible' explained. Which markers the researchers used (high remnant cholesterol and/or low-grade inflammation), what 'similar risk' means, and why this is a case for changing guidelines, not a new approval. Offer questions to bring to your doctor.
candidates.why_now: Presented at EASD this week and already picked up by Medical Xpress and News-Medical. 'Am I eligible?' is a top consumer search, and very few creators have covered this yet.

evidence.signal: People with BMI 25–26.9 plus high remnant cholesterol and/or inflammation had coronary heart disease risk similar to people eligible for GLP-1s (UK + Denmark data, EASD 2026)
Research makes a case for broader GLP-1 use to protect hearts

candidates.topic: CagriSema beat tirzepatide in REIMAGINE 5, but against the 5 mg tirzepatide dose (12.4% vs 9.1% weight loss at 60 weeks, type 2 diabetes)
candidates.angle: Read the fine print on the 'beats Zepbound' headlines: which doses were compared, who was in the trial (type 2 diabetes on metformin/SGLT2), and that A1C was similar (1.71% vs 1.67%, non-inferiority). Explain amylin plus GLP-1 in plain words.
candidates.why_now: Headlines today from The Hill and Pharmacy Times, plus Novo EASD presentations this week. Most coverage says 'outperforms Zepbound' without naming the doses, so a clearly differentiated angle is available.

evidence.signal: CagriSema 1.0/1.0 mg: 12.4% weight loss vs 9.1% with tirzepatide 5 mg at week 60; HbA1c non-inferior
CagriSema tops tirzepatide 5 mg in REIMAGINE 5
Trial population: adults with type 2 diabetes

candidates.topic: Stopping GLP-1s and heart risk: 333,000 US veterans with type 2 diabetes; gaps of 6+ months linked to higher heart attack/stroke/death risk, up to 22% after 2 years off (WashU)
candidates.angle: 'Metabolic whiplash' explained: what happens to blood pressure, cholesterol and inflammation when treatment stops. Observational, diabetes-only population. The takeaway is to plan any change with your prescriber, plus habits that help keep results. Not 'never stop'.
keywords: what happens when you stop GLP-1
candidates.why_now: Syndicated across dozens of Scripps local stations this weekend, plus Axios and ScienceDaily. 'Stopping Ozempic' is a huge evergreen search, and this is a fresh hook for it.

evidence.signal: 333,000+ veterans with type 2 diabetes; interruption linked to higher MACE risk, up to 22% after 2 years off
Stopping Ozempic may raise heart attack and stroke risk
The risks of stopping GLP-1s

candidates.topic: Oral GLP-1 orforglipron (Foundayo) linked to similar weight loss before, during and after menopause (ATTAIN-1/ATTAIN-2 post-hoc)
candidates.angle: 'Does menopause stop GLP-1s from working?' Answered with the subgroup data: 12.8–14.4% in ATTAIN-1 (no diabetes) and 8.9–13.6% in ATTAIN-2 (type 2 diabetes) at the highest dose, 72 weeks. Say it's a post-hoc subgroup analysis. Plus a myths-vs-facts on the pill vs the shot.
candidates.why_now: Medscape, Medical Xpress, News-Medical and HCPLive covered it over the last 48 hours. Foundayo is newly FDA-approved, and menopause + GLP-1 is one of the largest audience segments.

evidence.signal: Up to 14% weight loss in women at every menopause stage
Similar weight loss across three menopausal stages
ATTAIN-1: 12.8% / 14.4% / 14.1% (pre/peri/post) at 17.2 mg

candidates.topic: GLP-1s and sleep apnea: new JAMA Otolaryngology review finds 6–22 fewer breathing events per hour vs about 31 with CPAP
candidates.angle: 'Can I ditch my CPAP?' GLP-1s and CPAP work in different ways, so it can be both, not one or the other. Tirzepatide is approved for OSA with obesity. Anatomy also plays a part. Talk to your sleep doctor before changing anything.
candidates.why_now: The Hill syndicated it to 10+ Nexstar stations today. Sleep apnea is a key 'benefits beyond weight' pillar, and there's high consumer confusion about replacing CPAP.

evidence.signal: Review in JAMA Otolaryngology: GLP-1s reduce AHI, CPAP remains more effective
6–22 fewer events/hour vs about 31 with CPAP; strongest with tirzepatide

candidates.topic: Hair loss on GLP-1s: how common, why it happens (telogen effluvium from rapid weight loss), and what helps
candidates.angle: A calm, evidence-first explainer. The BMJ study found a modest relative increase with a low absolute risk. It's usually temporary shedding tied to fast weight loss. Protein, iron and not under-eating help, and see a clinician if it lasts. Refreshed by The Guardian and a Clin Dermatol review.
keywords: does hair grow back after Wegovy
candidates.why_now: The Guardian (Sep 27) and Times of India (Sep 28) ran it, plus a new Clin Dermatol review (Sep 21). One of the most-searched GLP-1 side-effect questions.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 use associated with modestly higher alopecia risk vs SGLT2/DPP-4; absolute risk low
Hair and scalp effects of GLP-1 receptor agonists in practice
Does GLP-1 use result in significant hair loss?

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and muscle: STEP UP MRI analysis of thigh muscle volume, fat inside muscle and physical function (Diabetes Obes Metab, Sep 20) + creatine commentary (Clin Nutr)
candidates.angle: 'Am I losing muscle on GLP-1?' Muscle quality (fat infiltration) and function, not just lean mass. Protein and strength training have the best evidence. Creatine is a promising but unproven add-on.
candidates.why_now: A fresh peer-reviewed secondary analysis from STEP UP and a Clin Nutr piece on creatine, both published in the last week. Mainstream coverage is minimal, and it fits our 'getting the most from GLP-1' pillar exactly.

evidence.signal: Effect of semaglutide on thigh skeletal muscle volume, fat infiltration and physical function (STEP UP)
Creatine for GLP-1-associated muscle loss

candidates.topic: Weight loss explains only about 20% of semaglutide's heart benefit (SELECT mediation, European Heart Journal) + who loses most weight (Diabetes Care)
candidates.angle: 'It's not just the scale.' Other pathways (inflammation, blood pressure, direct vascular effects) likely matter, in adults with established cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity. Pair it with the SELECT weight-predictor analysis.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 5 snapshots with stable momentum. News-Medical ran a fresh piece today ('researchers still cannot fully explain why'), and EASD adds heart data (Mounjaro CV).

evidence.signal: Semaglutide and cardiovascular risk reduction: a mediation analysis of SELECT
Predictors of peak body weight loss with semaglutide in SELECT

candidates.topic: GLP-1s and sudden vision loss (NAION): 216 lawsuits in the MDL. What the studies and regulators actually say
candidates.angle: Cut through the lawsuit headlines. The EMA lists NAION as a 'very rare' semaglutide side effect. Observational studies disagree on how big the risk is. Explain the warning signs (sudden painless vision loss in one eye) and why regular eye checks matter for people with diabetes. Don't tell anyone to stop their medicine.
candidates.why_now: New lawsuits reported by Boston.com, MassLive, Fox News, KOAT and NewsNation over the last 72 hours. High fear-driven search that needs a balanced, non-alarmist answer.

evidence.signal: Ozempic and Wegovy patients sue over alleged NAION vision loss
Drugmakers face lawsuits alleging GLP-1 medications caused sudden vision loss
Expert says GLP-1 vision loss claims will be 'hard to prove'

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and period changes: FDA adverse-event reports flag heavy bleeding, spotting and missed ovulation (a signal, not proof)
candidates.angle: What a 'disproportionality signal' means. Weight loss itself can change cycles, and ovulation can return (relevant to contraception and PCOS). Signals were narrower with tirzepatide and absent with liraglutide. Tell your clinician about cycle changes.
candidates.why_now: Yahoo Health (Sep 26) coverage plus a Cureus PCOS scoping review. Women's-health GLP-1 questions are under-served on YouTube.

evidence.signal: FAERS analysis: disproportionate reports of heavy menstrual bleeding, intermenstrual bleeding and anovulatory cycles with semaglutide
Reproductive and gynecologic effects of GLP-1 RAs in women with PCOS: scoping review

candidates.topic: Why GLP-1s don't work the same for everyone: 10–15% lose less than 5% in trials
candidates.angle: 'Not losing weight on GLP-1?' Covers what counts as a response, the factors researchers are studying (genetics, diabetes status, sex, adherence), and why it isn't a personal failure. Other benefits (blood sugar, heart) can still count. Discuss options with your prescriber.

candidates.why_now: DongA Science ran a new piece (Sep 27) on 'limited effect in up to 15%'. A big search question with a compassionate angle.

evidence.signal: Why some people don't lose weight with Wegovy (10–15% trial non-response)

candidates.angle: 'GLP-1s and your eyes: both sides.' Lower rates of new mild retinopathy (0.49% vs 1.2%) in an observational study, against the rare NAION signal. Why eye exams matter.

candidates.angle: Myth-check the 'Zepbound burns calories' headlines. What brown fat is, what the mouse study found, and why human data are needed. Appetite and food intake remain the main proven mechanism.
